AWS internship: remote, hands-on cloud projects

SkillMe's AWS internship is a 4-week remote cloud internship, open worldwide. You build a real serverless project on AWS with S3, Lambda, API Gateway and DynamoDB, one reviewed milestone a week, about 2–3 hours each. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

The Cloud and AWS internship in short

In the SkillMe Cloud and AWS internship you build one of 3 projects, such as CloudFolio: Serverless Portfolio Site with Contact Form, a project where you host your own portfolio website on AWS and add a working contact form powered by serverless functions. In week 1 you set up a cloud account the safe way, with a budget alert and a separate admin user, then host a simple portfolio website on Amazon S3. By week 4 you finish CloudFolio as a professional project: serve it over HTTPS through CloudFront, deploy site changes automatically from GitHub Actions, and document the architecture. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

What you build

One of 3 real projects, built over four weeks

You are assigned one of these projects when you start, and build it milestone by milestone.

CloudFolio: Serverless Portfolio Site with Contact Form

Host your own portfolio website on AWS and add a working contact form powered by serverless functions.

  1. W1Safe AWS Setup & Static Website on S3
  2. W2Contact Form API with Lambda & API Gateway
  3. W3Save Messages in DynamoDB with Least-Privilege Access
  4. W4HTTPS with CloudFront, Auto-Deploy & Architecture Diagram

SnapVault: Photo Sharing App on Cloud Storage

Build a simple photo gallery where people can upload pictures straight to cloud storage and view them on a web page.

  3. W3Photo Records in DynamoDB with S3 Event Triggers
  4. W4Infrastructure as Code with AWS SAM

LinkSnip: Serverless URL Shortener

  1. W1Safe AWS Setup & Landing Page on S3
  2. W2Shorten & Redirect with Lambda and API Gateway
  3. W3Store Links in DynamoDB & Handle Bad Input
  4. W4Click Analytics, Custom Aliases & Final Polish
Week by week

What each week of the Cloud and AWS internship covers

Shown for CloudFolio: Serverless Portfolio Site with Contact Form. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Safe AWS Setup & Static Website on S3

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Set up a cloud account the safe way, with a budget alert and a separate admin user, then host a simple portfolio website on Amazon S3. By the end of the week you will have a live website URL you built and deployed yourself.

    What you learn

    • What regions, services and the AWS Management Console are
    • Why you never use the root account day to day, and how IAM users and MFA protect you
    • Setting a budget alert so you are warned before spending any money
    • Storing files in S3 buckets and turning a bucket into a static website

    What you submit

    • A live portfolio website on an S3 website URL
    • A screenshot of your budget alert settings
    • A GitHub repo with the site code and README
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • A budget alert is active and sends email to you
    • You are signed in as an IAM user with MFA, not the root user
    • The portfolio loads in a browser from the S3 website endpoint
    • Only the website bucket is public; nothing else in the account is
    • The README has the live link and a screenshot

    Stretch goal: Upload the site from your terminal with the AWS CLI (or from AWS CloudShell) using aws s3 sync.

  2. Week 2 of 4

    Contact Form API with Lambda & API Gateway

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Make the contact form work using serverless: a small Lambda function receives the form data through an API Gateway URL. You will learn how code can run in the cloud without managing any server.

    What you learn

    • What serverless means and how an AWS Lambda function is triggered
    • Creating an HTTP API in API Gateway that calls a Lambda function
    • Reading request data and returning JSON responses from a Lambda handler
    • CORS: why browsers block requests to other domains and how to allow your site

    What you submit

    • A Lambda function that receives contact form data
    • An HTTP API with a POST /contact route
    • A live contact form that calls the API
    • A short demo video or screenshots
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • Submitting the form on the live site shows a success message
    • Each submission appears in the function's CloudWatch Logs
    • The API works from curl or Postman as well as the browser
    • The browser console shows no CORS errors

    Stretch goal: Add a honeypot field (a hidden input bots fill in) and ignore submissions where it is not empty.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    Save Messages in DynamoDB with Least-Privilege Access

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Store every contact message in a DynamoDB table and give your Lambda function only the permission it needs. You will also validate input and return clear errors, so the form behaves well when something goes wrong.

    What you learn

    • NoSQL basics with DynamoDB: tables, items and partition keys
    • Using the AWS SDK (boto3 or AWS SDK for JavaScript) inside Lambda
    • IAM roles and least-privilege policies for services
    • Input validation and proper HTTP error responses

    What you submit

    • A DynamoDB table storing contact messages
    • A least-privilege IAM policy for the Lambda role
    • Validation and error handling in the function and website
    • Screenshots of the table items and policy
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • Every valid form submission creates a new item in DynamoDB
    • The Lambda role can only write to this one table, not all of DynamoDB
    • An empty field or invalid email returns a 400 error shown on the page
    • A database failure returns a friendly error instead of a blank response
    • The README explains the data flow from form to database

    Stretch goal: Use Amazon SNS to email yourself whenever a new message arrives (remember to add sns:Publish to the role).

  4. Week 4 of 4

    HTTPS with CloudFront, Auto-Deploy & Architecture Diagram

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Finish CloudFolio as a professional project: serve it over HTTPS through CloudFront, deploy site changes automatically from GitHub Actions, and document the architecture. You will also clean up properly so nothing keeps costing money.

    What you learn

    • What a CDN is and how CloudFront gives your site HTTPS and faster loading
    • Deploying to S3 from GitHub Actions using repository secrets
    • Creating a separate, limited IAM user for automation
    • Drawing a cloud architecture diagram and cleaning up resources

    What you submit

    • The site served over HTTPS from CloudFront
    • A GitHub Actions workflow that deploys on every push
    • A README with an architecture diagram and cleanup steps
    • A 60-second demo video
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • The site loads over https:// from the CloudFront URL and the contact form works there
    • Pushing to main updates the live site automatically
    • The deploy user can only access your bucket and invalidations, and its keys exist only as GitHub secrets
    • The README includes an architecture diagram and a list of resources to delete
    • Your budget alert is still active and your bill shows no unexpected charges

    Stretch goal: Replace the access keys with GitHub OIDC so the workflow gets short-lived credentials from an IAM role instead.

Is it for you?

Who the Cloud and AWS internship is for, and what you leave with

This internship fits you if

  • You know the basics of AWS, Serverless and Storage and want a real project to show for it, not more tutorials.
  • You can start at beginner level. Week 1: Set up a cloud account the safe way, with a budget alert and a separate admin user, then host a simple portfolio website on Amazon S3.
  • You want to reach intermediate+ level in four weeks. Week 4: Finish CloudFolio as a professional project: serve it over HTTPS through CloudFront, deploy site changes automatically from GitHub Actions, and document the architecture.
  • You can give it about 2-3 hours a week around college or a job, from any country.

How to apply

  1. Take the 5-minute quiz. Eight questions on the basics of AWS, Serverless, Storage.

  3. Get shortlisted. If you are selected you hear back within 48 hours and receive your offer letter.
  4. Build and submit weekly. One milestone a week for four weeks, each one reviewed.

Cloud and AWS internship: questions and answers

What do you do in this AWS internship?

You build one serverless project on AWS: CloudFolio (a portfolio site with a contact form), SnapVault (a photo gallery on cloud storage) or LinkSnip (a URL shortener). Week 1 sets up a safe AWS account and a static site on S3; later weeks add Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB with least-privilege access, and CloudFront or AWS SAM.

Is the AWS internship remote?

Yes. The AWS internship is fully remote and open to students in any country. You work in your own AWS account at about 2–3 hours a week.

Do I need AWS experience for this AWS cloud internship?

No. Week 1 starts at beginner level with a safe account setup. A 5-minute screening quiz checks you have the basics.

What will I build in the Cloud and AWS internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: CloudFolio: Serverless Portfolio Site with Contact Form, SnapVault: Photo Sharing App on Cloud Storage or LinkSnip: Serverless URL Shortener. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the Cloud and AWS internship?

The Cloud and AWS internship works with AWS, Serverless and Storage. Week 1: what regions, services and the AWS Management Console are; why you never use the root account day to day, and how IAM users and MFA protect you. Week 2: what serverless means and how an AWS Lambda function is triggered; creating an HTTP API in API Gateway that calls a Lambda function. Week 3: NoSQL basics with DynamoDB: tables, items and partition keys; using the AWS SDK (boto3 or AWS SDK for JavaScript) inside Lambda. Week 4: what a CDN is and how CloudFront gives your site HTTPS and faster loading; deploying to S3 from GitHub Actions using repository secrets.

Do I need experience to apply for the Cloud and AWS internship?

You need the basics of AWS, Serverless and Storage, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you set up a cloud account the safe way, with a budget alert and a separate admin user, then host a simple portfolio website on Amazon S3. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each Cloud and AWS milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of CloudFolio: Serverless Portfolio Site with Contact Form, that means: a budget alert is active and sends email to you; you are signed in as an IAM user with MFA, not the root user; the portfolio loads in a browser from the S3 website endpoint; only the website bucket is public; nothing else in the account is; the README has the live link and a screenshot. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the Cloud and AWS internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Set up a secure AWS account with MFA, an IAM admin user and a budget alert; Hosted my personal portfolio as a static website on Amazon S3; Learned cloud basics including regions, buckets and access policies; Built a serverless contact form API using AWS Lambda and API Gateway; Connected a static website to a cloud API with fetch and CORS; Debugged cloud functions using CloudWatch Logs; Stored contact form submissions in Amazon DynamoDB from a Lambda function; Wrote a least-privilege IAM policy so the function can only write to one table; Added input validation and clear error responses to a serverless API; Built CloudFolio, a serverless portfolio on AWS with S3, CloudFront, Lambda, API Gateway and DynamoDB; Automated deployments to S3 and CloudFront with GitHub Actions; Documented the system with an architecture diagram and a cost-safe cleanup plan.

What are the other projects in the Cloud and AWS internship?

SnapVault: Photo Sharing App on Cloud Storage: Build a simple photo gallery where people can upload pictures straight to cloud storage and view them on a web page. LinkSnip: Serverless URL Shortener: Build your own link shortener, like a mini bit.ly, that turns long links into short ones and counts the clicks. Every project follows the same four-week shape, with one reviewed milestone a week.

Is the Cloud and AWS internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based: 8–10 interns are picked each month from those who complete the internship and hold an issued certificate. It is not paid to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
